bug: A reentrant checkpoint reader could accept a result or cloned error already owned by an active read. Per-call cleanup registries did not prevent overlapping ownership.

before.observations: Nested reads were accepted instead of returning a boundary failure at seven root-result and three shared-error reentry points.

fix: Reserve the root result before inspecting caller metadata, and reserve cloned errors before reading their cleanup methods.
Reject overlapping acquisition through this module without reading or freeing the active handle; retain reservations through cleanup and release them in finally.
Allow independent nested reads and release reservations when invalid protected-owner metadata leaves ownership with the caller.
Consolidate three identical UTF-8 length validators into one internal helper, preserving encoding and byte-limit semantics without increasing release budgets.

scenarios: Closing a checkpoint store settles loads queued behind a blocked database deletion.
An explicit checkpoint survives a real page reload, including Undo and Redo.
An explicit session backup restores typed values and the redo frontier through Rust.

limits: Reservations protect overlapping calls within the checkpoint reader module, not unrelated adapters or separately loaded module instances.
They are not a persistent consumed-handle registry: callers must still never reuse a freed generated handle.
Browser integration verifies normal persistence behavior; synthetic unit handles reproduce getter/destructor reentry.
No durable format, Rust implementation, package version or size limit changed.
The separate WebKit numeric fault remains unresolved; native instrumentation stayed paused.
No full release qualification, commit, push or publication is claimed.
